_readme: Design-system allowlist (docs/design-system.md §7): the only drift the guards accept. tests/ci/ds-guard, colour-guard and type-guard fail on any count outside it, and on an entry above its file's count (lower it: DS_ALLOWLIST=lower npx jest -i ds-guard colour-guard type-guard). An entry is { metric, file, count, list, reason }: the list says which kind of exception it is, the reason says why this file needs it.

lists.off-scale: A raw value with no exact token. Swapping it for the nearest --sp-* / --fs-* token would move or resize things, so it waits for the page PR that owns the screen (with screenshots).
lists.cascade: An !important or #id selector that decides which rule wins today: the billing page's #billing layer, desktop overrides of JS-set inline display, and utility hides. Removing it needs its own cascade-checked PR.
lists.js-state: A template's initial style="display:..." that JS reads and toggles through element.style (billing mode, Today tabs, Insights sections). Tests and desktop.css [style*="none"] selectors read it too: these are the remaining test hooks.
lists.standalone: Styling for output that cannot use app.css tokens: the exported HTML file, DevTools console styling, and the quota banner, which styles itself so it shows even when the app's CSS did not load.
lists.print: Output for paper: canvases sent to the thermal printer or saved as a printable image stay black on white in every theme, like @media print and the receipt files (which the guards skip).
lists.canvas: Chart colours drawn on <canvas> and the legend swatches that key them: a fixed palette, the same in every theme, because a canvas cannot follow CSS tokens.
lists.share-text: Text that leaves the app (the WhatsApp day report and due reminders), where the emoji is part of the message, not a UI icon.
lists.proper-noun: Title Case that names a page or a theme (Open Outstanding, Open Today, Modern Minimal): page and theme names are capitalised as in the navigation.
lists.visible-fix: Real drift whose fix changes what the owner sees (an emoji to swap for a sprite icon). It stays until the page PR that owns the screen makes that change.
